title: Fixed-ended beam with three point loads

source.work: McGuire, W., Gallagher, R. H., Ziemian, R. D., Matrix Structural Analysis
source.notes: input data and targets read on the cited pages; nothing of the source is reproduced

analysis: Plane (x-y) problem of the source modelled in 3D with the global Y axis vertical, so that the source's x, y and theta_z are the model's X, Y and rz. In-plane bending is about local z for every member (default orientation), hence the source's I is the section's Iz. Beam of 8 m, both ends fixed, I = 200e6 mm^4, E = 200,000 MPa, nodes every 2 m. Loads 50, 30 and 10 kN downward at x = 2, 4 and 6 m. First order, no shear deformation. Section properties the source does not give because they do not enter its plane model (Iy, J; A where stated) are placeholders that do not influence the targets.

quarantine.diagnosis: 5 of 6 targets reproduced (v1, theta1, v2, theta2, v3). Missed: theta3, engine 1.4375e-3 rad, printed 1.48e-3 rad (2.9 % apart, tolerance 0.34 %). Suspected misprint or arithmetic slip in the source. Evidence: the source's own substructure equations give 1.4375e-3 - with its printed matrices, theta3 = -(1/4)(1.5e-3 x v2 + theta2) = -(1/4)(1.5e-3 x (-4.0) + 0.25e-3) = 1.4375e-3 rad for the printed v2 = -4.0 mm and theta2 = 0.25e-3 rad. The engine's results for this model are confirmed by the other tiers that apply (tier C: OpenSeesPy and PyNite agree with the engine; tier D: equilibrium and the other invariants pass); the difference is between the source's printed digits and the exact solution of the stated problem.
